transcript.content: Hello, I am the physician attending to you today. What symptoms are you experiencing?
"Hello Doc, it started off just being nagging after sitting for too long but has gotten worse lately. My hands especially feel kinda wobbly when trying to grab things from high shelves."
Do you experience any numbness or tingling sensations in your hands?

Yes, I have been having trouble holding onto things lately because my fingers hurt when they move too much during certain tasks around the house. It feels better after sitting down for some time though. Walking has become harder on me; I need extra support just taking short walks outside now. Whenever I get up from bed at nighttime, it takes longer than before until everything loosens up enough so I don't feel all clumsy moving about throughout my day. Things aren't quite fitting right into cabinets anymore — knobs seem farther apart sometimes...and yes, if someone were tickling near where these little pimples showed up next to nails here - well let's say touching them causes dis
Have you noticed any changes in your vision or hearing?

As for my eyesight, I haven't had much trouble recently; things have been pretty clear when reading small print without needing glasses most times now. And about hearing—unless it was during yesterday's storm, I didn't notice anything off then either.
Have you noticed any changes in your sense of taste or smell?

No, I haven't really thought about my nose much lately; it seems normal for me. My hands have been giving me some trouble though – they feel achy after doing chores around the house all day long, especially when climbing up to fix things on high shelves or opening jars. There was this one time last week where my wrist started hurting just from turning keys without even lifting them too far off the table! It doesn't seem serious because when I take breaks between tasks, it eases right back down. Based on the patient's symptoms of joint pain, stiffness, and difficulty with fine motor skills, as well as their age (65 years old), the final diagnosis is likely osteoarthritis. Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease that affects the cartilage surrounding the joints, leading to inflammation, pain, and limited mobility. The patient's description of feeling better after resting and their history of recent gardening activities are also consistent with this diagnosis.
